comments.text:
That is actually pretty common around the world.
You see, there are two types of employment contracts. Indefinite and Fixed-Term. Fixed-Term, give your employer the power to fire you at any given time during this period or at the end of it.
Indefinite, on the other hand, doesn't. The only way to "fire" an employee on Indefinite is to either make them quit or fully legally erase his job post from the company. So you're not firing him, you're just removing that job post. Or find that person legally incompetent

Pretty wild.

comments.text:
Btw for anyone interested:

1. It is Psychological Harassment / Workplace Bullying

In many jurisdictions, isolating an employee and forcing them into extreme, enforced boredom ("boreout") is legally classified as psychological harassment. Forcing a human being to sit in silence without stimulation while actively monitoring them to ensure they don't look at or do something is an abusive, toxic work environment designed to inflict mental distress.

2. It is a Total Breach of Contract

When a company hires you, they sign a contract to give you work in exchange for pay. By intentionally giving you zero tasks, they have breached their end of the employment agreement.

3. It is the Definition of Constructive Dismissal

Because they are making your day-to-day life humiliating and unbearable, the law does not look at this as you simply sitting there. If you are forced to resign because of this psychological torture, courts will treat it as a constructive dismissal (meaning they essentially fired you anyway). This allows you to sue for wrongful termination and claim unemployment benefits.
